questions.q: Why does Rubin say outer order matters?
a: It raises your mood and confidence to take on challenges
It proves you are more disciplined than others
It saves money by avoiding new purchases
It impresses guests and family members
questions.why: Lesson 1 says pleasing our senses with order lifts our spirits and builds confidence.

questions.q: What three questions does Rubin suggest asking about each object?
a: Do I need it, love it or use it
Did I pay a lot of money for it
Will someone else want to own it
Does it match the rest of the room
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests asking whether each object is needed, loved or used.

questions.q: How does Rubin handle unfinished projects?
a: Finish them or abandon them to clear the guilt
Keep them visible until they are done
Move them into a storage room
Give them to a friend to finish
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the easiest way to finish a project can be to abandon it.

questions.q: What state does Rubin say you should be in when decluttering?
a: Rested, unhurried and not hungry
Energetic, rushed and focused
Angry enough to be ruthless
Surrounded by family for votes
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises decluttering while rested, unhurried and not hungry.

questions.q: How does Rubin suggest preventing clutter from returning?
a: Put things away daily and carry items toward their home
Do one large clean at the start of each season
Buy storage boxes for everything you own
Avoid buying anything new for a year
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends daily habits, like carrying items toward their proper place.
